meanings.note: Adverb meaning 'together', often pronounced 가치.

examples.trans: Let's go together.
Let's go together. (2)

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Let's pay off together today.
I worked hard to pay off yesterday too.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Used as noun (글).

examples.trans: Wait—the card says they love you! Did you not know? Cindy uploaded a post!

examples.text: 너네 이제 이상한 글 쓰면 내가 다 지워버릴 거야!
examples.trans: From now on, the moment any of you write nasty posts, I am deleting every single one!

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Colloquial spoken form of 너희네; used among close friends or to juniors.

examples.text: 너네 오늘 수업 몇 시에 끝나?
examples.trans: What time does your class end today?
You guys all come over here together.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.
Did you hear about this a few days?
I was busy today because of a few days.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Used as nominalized -기 (무르기).

examples.text: 콜! 너 무르기 없기다, 20%라고 네가 분명히 얘기했어!
examples.trans: Deal! No take-backs—you clearly just said twenty percent!
Let us do that (backing out, take-backs) right away.

meanings.note: Literal meaning: steamed rice.
By extension, refers to a meal in everyday expressions like 밥 먹다 ('to eat a meal').

examples.trans: Have you eaten?
Today's lunch is delicious.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (분명히).

examples.text: 그게 분명히 차에 태워서 출발을 했는데 운전하다가 돌아보니까 사라져 있더래요.
examples.trans: Well, he swears he put her in the van and pulled out, yet when he looked back while driving she had vanished.

examples.text: 바쁘고 힘든 부분도 분명히 있다는 거 잘 알지만 분명 좋은 부분도 있다고 생각합니다.
examples.trans: I know well there are busy, exhausting parts, yet I believe there are unmistakably good parts too.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.
Did you hear about this news and?
I was busy today because of news and.
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.
Chew it thoroughly. It is a hangover pancake.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 씹다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (chew).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 변 대표랑 준모랑 서로 쌍소리 오가고 촬영장 아주 개판 됐대요.
examples.trans: They say CEO Byun and Joon-mo traded harsh words and the set turned into a total mess.
Here the word for 'completely' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
Did you hear about this anti-fan forum?
I was busy today because of anti-fan forum.

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Hey, Baek Seung-chan, are you just getting back now?
Here the word for 'hey' is key.

meanings.note: Used as exclamatory adverb (어쩜).

examples.text: 근데 신디 걔는 며칠을 같이 지냈는데 어쩜 잘 들어갔다는 소식이 없냐? 은혜도 모르는 아주 왕싸가지야!
examples.trans: Still, Cindy stayed here for days—how has she sent zero word that she got back safely? What an ungrateful brat!
I thought it over again (how on earth).

meanings.note: Used as idiomatic subject (어처구니가).

examples.text: 나보고 신디 안티카페 운영진이 되라고? 어처구니가 없다 진짜!
examples.trans: They are asking me to become a moderator of Cindy's anti-fan cafe?! That is beyond ridiculous!
This point about absurdity (idiom) is really important.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word.

examples.trans: Let's go watch a movie.
What movie is it?

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: Used as slang noun + casual copula (왕싸가지야!).

examples.text: 근데 신디 걔는 며칠을 같이 지냈는데 어쩜 잘 들어갔다는 소식이 없냐? 은혜도 모르는 아주 왕싸가지야!

meanings.note: Used as noun + complement (운영진이).

examples.text: 나보고 신디 안티카페 운영진이 되라고? 어처구니가 없다 진짜!

meanings.note: Used as noun + -도 (은혜도).

examples.trans: Still, Cindy stayed here for days—how has she sent zero word that she got back safely? What an ungrateful brat!

meanings.note: Describes something unusual or out of the ordinary.
Used when sensing something is wrong.

examples.trans: The computer sounds a bit strange.
It's suspicious that he's suddenly being so nice.

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used as quotative question (적적하다고?).

examples.text: 신디가 활동을 안 하니까 씹을 사람이 없어서 적적하다고? 어이가 없네 진짜!
examples.trans: They say life feels lonely with nobody to trash while Cindy is off the air? Unbelievable!
It is really they feel lonely compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

colloquial

meanings.note: Used as percentage + -로 (85%로).

examples.trans: So far, "it was intentional" is winning overwhelmingly at eighty-five percent.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?

examples.trans: If we settle it that way, I will give you a ten percent discount!
Let us do that (discount) right away.

meanings.note: Contrasted with 신용카드 (credit card).

examples.trans: I will pay in cash.

meanings.note: Used as noun + instrumental (현물로).

examples.text: 저 이제 현금 말고 현물로 결제해 주시면 안 되겠습니까? 밥이라든가 술이라든가 영화 티켓이라든가!

examples.text: 예전에 이상한 사이트에서 활동을 한 적이 있다거나?
examples.trans: Or were you ever active on any shady websites in the past?
